stance.role: Senior Software Engineer <muted>— distributed systems, payments, AI agents</muted>
stance.lede: I design from the failure path first — before the happy path is fast, I want to know what the system does when:

network.title: The network doesn’t answer
network.text: Did the payment leave? A retry must never pay twice.

race.title: Two requests arrive at once
race.text: Check-then-write leaves a gap. Only one of them may win.

model.title: A model isn’t sure
model.text: Confident and wrong is the expensive case. Below the threshold, a person answers.

capabilities.title: What I build
capabilities.note: Production systems end to end — from the transaction to the screen.

ai.title: AI agents and RAG
ai.text: Voice and chat agents grounded in the product’s own data: retrieval per client, output checked against a schema, a confidence threshold and a human hand-off. Plus MCP servers that put a platform inside clients’ own AI tools.

backend.title: Distributed backends
backend.text: Services that stay consistent under concurrency: transactions, idempotency, queues, retries and reconciliation.

payments.title: Payments and money flows
payments.text: Wallets, deposits, payouts and e‑signatures — where a duplicate costs money.

realtime.title: Real-time systems
realtime.text: Live balances, statuses and dashboards that don’t drift from the source of truth.

automation.title: Automation and integrations
automation.text: Anything people repeat becomes a pipeline: browser automation, document workflows, scheduled jobs, bots and third-party APIs.

frontend.title: Frontend and mobile
frontend.text: Microfrontends, SSR, design systems and React Native apps for large products.

admin.title: Admin and operations
admin.text: Moderation, financial operations, RBAC and analytics for internal teams.

cases.note: Diagrams are simplified; confidence values are illustrative.

payouts.title: Paying out exactly once over a network that may not answer
payouts.metric_label: concurrent workers, no second transaction on retry
payouts.situation: Financial infrastructure was the most critical part of a crypto platform. Four ways it could lose money:

order.effect: one gap stalls every later tx

sequential.title: Sequential processing
sequential.note: kept order, but one stuck tx blocked the queue

memory.title: Nonce counter in memory
memory.note: lost on restart, broke with several instances

transaction.title: Nonce and signing in one DB transaction
transaction.note: if signing fails, the nonce rolls back — no gap

resend.title: Store the signed tx before sending, resend the same one
resend.note: the network executes it only once

reconcile.title: Reconciliation on start and on schedule

payouts.result: 1000+ workers in production. A retry after a timeout never created a second transaction; restarts lost neither nonce nor state.
payouts.quote: The point wasn’t adding workers — it was separating what can run in parallel from what can’t.

claims.title: One order, one courier — at peak hour
claims.situation: A free order was visible to several couriers, and at peak they accepted it almost at the same moment.

check.title: Check, then write
check.note: a second request slipped in between

lock.title: Redis as the only lock
lock.note: keys could expire and drift from the database

conditional.title: Conditional write in a PostgreSQL transaction

idempotent.title: Repeat from the same courier counts as success
idempotent.note: a bad network gives no false refusal

filter.title: Redis as a fast filter
filter.note: needless requests never reach the database

push.title: Taken orders leave lists over WebSocket

claims.result: No more double assignments. Repeat claims at peak dropped by 86%, and a repeat tap no longer shows a false refusal.
claims.quote: Correctness and speed are separate concerns. The remaining 14% are taps on taken orders from a stale screen.

normal.outcome: outcome: order assigned to courier A

agent.title: A voice agent that knows when to hand off
agent.situation: Support and ad-scenario preparation for B2B clients depended on people.

rag.title: RAG with a per-client filter and confidence threshold
rag.note: not enough data — a person takes over

streaming.title: Streaming voice over LiveKit
streaming.note: replies start early and can be interrupted

schema.title: Schema validation and client confirmation
schema.note: a model error never reaches a campaign

evals.title: Eval set of test questions
evals.note: prompt changes can’t silently degrade answers

agent.result: B2B campaign throughput grew by 32%. The scenario is assembled during the conversation; when data is missing, the call goes to a person.
agent.quote: The key was limiting where the model can be wrong. A high threshold calls a person more often — better than a confident wrong answer.

normal.outcome: outcome: scenario confirmed by the client

items.wallet: Designed a concurrent wallet system on Python asyncio — <metric>1000+</metric> coroutine workers, nonce sequencing in PostgreSQL, idempotent retries and crash recovery.
items.claim: Reworked an order-claim service with transactional logic over PostgreSQL and Redis — duplicate acceptances at peak <metric>−86%</metric>.
items.sync: Built real-time balance and campaign-lifecycle sync on NestJS, gRPC and PostgreSQL — desync incidents <metric>−43%</metric>, p95 update latency <plain>under 250 ms</plain>.
items.orders: Kept order workflows between ingestion and execution at <metric>99.3%</metric> reliability with reconciliation, retry policies and state validation.
items.drafts: Resolved conflicts in collaborative campaign drafts with optimistic locking in PostgreSQL — inconsistencies <metric>−38%</metric>.

items.voice: Built the backend of a voice agent on RAG and LiveKit that turns a spoken brief into a validated ad scenario — campaign throughput <metric>+32%</metric>.
items.mcp: Created a Python MCP server so B2B clients run routine platform tasks from their own AI tools — onboarding and support <metric>7h → 1h</metric>.
items.proofs: Replaced manual proof collection with a Playwright and S3 pipeline producing screenshots and Excel reports — manual work <metric>−78%</metric>.
items.esign: Shipped an e‑signature service with DocuSign and Stripe on AWS EKS — document processing from <metric>days to minutes</metric>, 99.9% SLA.

items.mfe: Led the move from a frontend monolith to Module Federation microfrontends — release cycle <metric>−47%</metric>, production bugs <metric>−33%</metric>.
items.dashboard: Optimised a real-time dashboard for <plain>1M</plain> NFT positions with WebSockets, layered caching and virtualisation — render time <metric>−64%</metric>.
items.deposits: Delivered unified fiat and crypto deposits and withdrawals with MetaMask and WalletConnect — completion rate <metric>+22%</metric>.
items.ssr: Moved high-traffic pages from CSR to SSR on Next.js — TTFB <metric>−31%</metric>, FCP <metric>−37%</metric>.
items.pwa: Added offline mode to a courier PWA with service workers and background sync — stale balance displays <metric>−41%</metric>.

about.title: About
about.note: The path, how I work, and what I think about outside the code.

path.title: The path
path.first: I started on the frontend and spent years there — which is why I still care how a backend decision lands on the screen. Then I moved down the stack: backends, payments, real-time systems. Now most of my time goes where distributed systems meet AI.
path.second: The work I like best is the kind where a mistake is expensive: orders, money, documents. And anything people do by hand more than twice, I’d rather turn into a system.

work.title: How I work with people and the business

autonomy.title: Autonomy, end to end
autonomy.text: I take a direction from requirements to release on my own, and bring the hard architecture calls to the team.

business.title: Business thinking
business.text: I judge work by the number it moves — completion rate, throughput, hours saved — and care how the product makes money.

writing.title: Decisions in writing
writing.text: Large tasks get decomposed, API contracts agreed up front, trade-offs written down before code.

bridging.title: Bridging teams
bridging.text: Aligning frontend, backend and product; at home in distributed, async, international teams.

psychology.title: Psychology
psychology.text: cognitive biases and how people actually make decisions.

systems.title: Systems thinking
systems.text: philosophy and the hidden dependencies in social systems.

products.title: Building products
products.text: small AI-first products of my own, end to end.

build.title: How I build
build.note: AI agents write a lot of my code — inside a harness I assembled from open-source tools, so the result is checked by the system rather than by hope. Spec first, tests first, rules enforced before commit.
build.harness_title: The harness — the wrapper I build around coding agents
